extension.description: Open or attach to tmux sessions named after the current workspace folder, in a dedicated terminal view in the Secondary Side Bar.
view.terminal.name: Terminal
config.notifyOnBell: Show a notification when a tmux session's terminal bell rings (e.g. an AI CLI needs your attention).
config.notifySound: Play a sound alongside the bell notification, so you notice it even away from the screen. On by default.
config.notifyToast: Show the pop-up notification (toast) when a session rings the bell. On by default; turn it off to keep only the sound. To silence both, set `notifyOnBell` to false instead.
config.notifySoundPreset: Which sound to play when the bell notification fires. Preview each one by changing this setting and triggering a bell.
config.notifySoundPresetOnAsk: Which sound to play when the bell is an "ask" (waiting for your input, e.g. a permission prompt) rather than a completed turn. Requires the reference bell-reason hook script (see the README); without it every bell uses the plain sound preset. Defaults to Siren Sweep so it stands out from the completion sound.
config.notifyBridgeStatusline: Append the session's context usage and cost to the bell notification, read from the statusline bridge file. Requires the reference `tmux-opener-statusline.sh` (see the README); has no effect without it. On by default.
config.terminal.fontFamily: Font family for the Tmux terminal view. Choose the first (empty) option to inherit the integrated terminal's font family. Each option carries a `monospace` fallback; a font not installed on your OS falls back to it. A custom value set in settings.json still works even if it isn't in this list.
config.terminal.fontFamily.editorDefault: Inherit the integrated terminal's font family (`terminal.integrated.fontFamily`), falling back to `Menlo, Monaco, "Courier New", monospace` when that is unset too. The editor's own font is deliberately not inherited — it may be proportional or serif, which a terminal cannot use.
config.terminal.fontFamily.bundled: Use the M PLUS 1 Code Term font, M PLUS 1 Code refitted so that no symbol a terminal draws one cell wide is ever squashed sideways: an outline wider than 1.15 cells is scaled down to that width, and any outline reaching past its cell is centred, so the overhang is the same on both sides and at most about 7.6% of a cell (the ratio alone puts it at 7.5%; integer rounding on this typeface's 500-unit cell accounts for the rest, measured). Symbols may therefore touch the neighbouring cell slightly, but never reach the width at which the renderer squashes them. Height is not scaled by the same factor as width: a refitted glyph's height is scaled by up to 1.3 times its width factor, capped per glyph so the stretch never carries it past the top or bottom edge of the face's own 漢 — so symbols read at their proper size and the refit pushes nothing past that kanji (measured: 0 glyphs newly outside its box; this is not a claim that nothing reaches further than 漢, since 27 of the 46 refitted glyphs in the regular face were outside it to begin with and were left untouched). Glyphs with no room left are left alone, so not every refitted symbol is taller (19 of the 46 refitted glyphs in the regular face and 25 of 67 in the bold grew, measured). The cell grid itself does not move — one column, and a full-width character, are the same widths as before — and in this typeface the refit changes no advance at all (measured), because upstream already draws these symbols one column wide, so only ink moves. ASCII and Latin-1 are left as the typeface designed them. What the refit does NOT do is add a glyph — it only moves ink that is already in the file, so a character the typeface never drew is still not drawn by it. That matters here more than in the other bundled fonts: of the 26 everyday symbols this project samples, this typeface has 7, and the other 19 (`①` `★` `⚠` `Ⓐ` among them) are absent (measured with `scripts/font-fit/survey.py` against the shipped TTFs), so whatever your OS picks draws them — usually not one cell wide. The remedy is a second font rather than a better refit: set `tmuxOpener.terminal.fontFallback` to a family that does have those characters, and only they are drawn from it. Measured in headless Chromium at 100px, where one cell is 50.0px: with no fallback `①` `★` `⚠` `Ⓐ` advance 89.6 / 60.2 / 60.2 / 100.0px; with `Mgen+ 1mn Term` as the fallback all four advance 50.0px, and `A` is 50.0px either way. This requires the dedicated M PLUS 1 Code Term font extension; when it isn't installed the terminal falls back to your OS's default monospace font (no OS install needed). It includes Japanese glyphs, so Japanese text renders in the same font.
config.terminal.fontFamily.mgenplus1mn: Use the Mgen+ 1mn Term font, Mgen+ 1mn refitted so that no symbol a terminal draws one cell wide is ever squashed sideways: an outline wider than 1.15 cells is scaled down to that width, and any outline reaching past its cell is centred, so the overhang is the same on both sides and at most about 7.5% of a cell. Symbols may therefore touch the neighbouring cell slightly, but never reach the width at which the renderer squashes them. Height is not scaled by the same factor as width: a refitted glyph's height is scaled by up to 1.3 times its width factor, capped per glyph so the stretch never carries it past the top or bottom edge of the face's own 漢 — so symbols read at their proper size and the refit pushes nothing past that kanji (measured: 0 glyphs newly outside its box; this is not a claim that nothing reaches further than 漢, since 141 of the 1001 refitted glyphs in the regular face were outside it to begin with and were left untouched). Glyphs with no room left are left alone, so not every refitted symbol is taller (857 of the 1001 refitted glyphs in the regular face and 899 of 1020 in the bold grew, measured). The cell grid itself does not move — one column, and a full-width character, are the same widths as before — and ASCII and Latin-1 are left as the typeface designed them. A refitted symbol's advance is set to one column too, which is what puts it in a single cell — upstream draws nearly all of them full-width (997 of the 1001 refitted glyphs in the regular face, 1016 of 1020 in the bold, measured); the few upstream already drew one column wide keep the advance they had, and only their ink moves. This requires the dedicated Mgen+ 1mn Term font extension; when it isn't installed the terminal falls back to your OS's default monospace font (no OS install needed). It includes Japanese glyphs, so Japanese text renders in the same font.
config.terminal.fontFamily.roundedMgenpl: Use the Rounded Mgen+ 1mn Term font, a rounded-corner variant of Mgen+ 1mn refitted so that no symbol a terminal draws one cell wide is ever squashed sideways: an outline wider than 1.15 cells is scaled down to that width, and any outline reaching past its cell is centred, so the overhang is the same on both sides and at most about 7.5% of a cell. Height is not scaled by the same factor as width: a refitted glyph's height is scaled by up to 1.3 times its width factor, capped per glyph so the stretch never carries it past the top or bottom edge of the face's own 漢 — so symbols read at their proper size and the refit pushes nothing past that kanji (measured: 0 glyphs newly outside its box; this is not a claim that nothing reaches further than 漢, since 131 of the 1000 refitted glyphs in the regular face were outside it to begin with and were left untouched). Glyphs with no room left are left alone, so not every refitted symbol is taller (868 of the 1000 refitted glyphs in the regular face and 896 of 1019 in the bold grew, measured). The cell grid itself does not move — one column, and a full-width character, are the same widths as before — and ASCII and Latin-1 are left as the typeface designed them. A refitted symbol's advance is set to one column too, which is what puts it in a single cell — upstream draws nearly all of them full-width (997 of the 1000 refitted glyphs in the regular face, 1016 of 1019 in the bold, measured); the few upstream already drew one column wide keep the advance they had, and only their ink moves. This requires the dedicated Rounded Mgen+ 1mn Term font extension; when it isn't installed the terminal falls back to your OS's default monospace font (no OS install needed). It includes Japanese glyphs, so Japanese text renders in the same font.
config.terminal.fontFamily.plemoljpConso: Use the PlemolJP Console HS font. This requires the dedicated PlemolJP Console HS font extension; when it isn't installed the terminal falls back to your OS's default monospace font (no OS install needed). It includes Japanese glyphs, so Japanese text renders in the same font. It is the one bundled font shipped exactly as its upstream publishes it: unlike the four Term fonts in this list it has not been refitted for terminal cells, because upstream already draws the East Asian Ambiguous symbols in everyday use (● ○ ■ ★ ✓ … ①) on a one-cell advance rather than a fullwidth one. What it lacks is the refit's guarantee, which is a bound rather than containment: the Term fonts also let a symbol reach a little past its cell, but never far enough to be squashed. Here some codepoints stay fullwidth (⚠, the enclosed letters Ⓐ-Ⓩ, the dingbat digits ❶-❿, and others) — handed a single cell, those are squashed sideways. Others are one cell wide with an outline reaching past it, by more than the refit would allow (① overhangs about 8.3% of a cell on each side in the regular face, 9.7% in the bold, against the refit's 7.5% ceiling), so they are drawn over the neighbouring cell.
config.terminal.fontFamily.shirokumagenT: Use the ShirokumaGen Term font, HackGen Console refitted so that no symbol a terminal draws one cell wide is ever squashed sideways: an outline wider than 1.15 cells is scaled down to that width, and any outline reaching past its cell is centred, so the overhang is the same on both sides and at most about 7.6% of a cell (the ratio alone puts it at 7.5%; integer rounding on this typeface's 540-unit cell accounts for the rest, measured). Symbols may therefore touch the neighbouring cell slightly, but never reach the width at which the renderer squashes them. Height is not scaled by the same factor as width: a refitted glyph's height is scaled by up to 1.3 times its width factor, capped per glyph so the stretch never carries it past the top or bottom edge of the face's own 漢 — so symbols read at their proper size and the refit pushes nothing past that kanji (measured: 0 glyphs newly outside its box; this is not a claim that nothing reaches further than 漢, since 593 of the 1723 refitted glyphs in the regular face were outside it to begin with and keep the shape equal scaling gives them — which is a statement about the vertical factor, not about the bytes: all 593 are refitted, 573 of them had their advance set to one column, and only 8 are unchanged to the unit against upstream, measured). Glyphs with no room left are left alone, so not every refitted symbol is taller (1128 of the 1723 refitted glyphs in the regular face and 1115 of 1694 in the bold grew, measured). The cell grid itself does not move — one column, and a full-width character, are the same widths as before — and ASCII and Latin-1 are left as the typeface designed them. A refitted symbol's advance is set to one column too, which is what puts it in a single cell: upstream draws these on the fullwidth advance, so 1656 glyphs in the regular face and 1621 in the bold go from 1080 to 540 (measured), and no other advance in the file changes. Of the bundled fonts this one covers the most codepoints (18,201 in the regular face, measured), and all 26 of the everyday symbols this project samples are present in it — worth knowing because a refit can move glyphs but never add one. This requires the dedicated ShirokumaGen Term font extension; when it isn't installed the terminal falls back to your OS's default monospace font (no OS install needed). It includes Japanese glyphs, so Japanese text renders in the same font.
config.terminal.fontFallback: A second font family, used only for characters the font chosen above has no glyph for. While that font is available, the terminal renders with `<Font Family>, <this>, monospace`, and the browser picks per character: anything the first font has is drawn by the first font, so ordinary text is unchanged. It helps only where the fallback family actually has the character — if neither font has it, your OS decides what draws it, exactly as before. When the chosen font is NOT available (its font extension is not installed, or its regular face did not load in time), the terminal renders with the editor's own font instead — that value already ends in a generic monospace, so this family is only consulted after it and the effect is weaker: measured in headless Chromium at 100px, where one cell is 50.0px, `①` and `Ⓐ` still reached the fallback (89.6 / 100.0 -> 50.0px) while `★` and `⚠` stayed at 60.2px, drawn by the OS monospace that has them. The default (empty) leaves everything as it is today. Set the second family HERE rather than typing it into Font Family by hand: only a value in this setting is kept out of the extension's font-identity checks (which family you selected, which face to load before the cell grid is measured), and those checks pick the LONGEST registered family name found in the value — so a second family hand-written into Font Family with a longer name than the first (`"Mgen+ 1mn Term", "Rounded Mgen+ 1mn Term"`) can be taken for the one you selected. Choosing a bundled family requires that family's own font extension; without it this setting simply has no effect.
config.terminal.fontFallback.none: No fallback family. Characters the chosen font lacks are left to your OS — the behaviour before this setting existed.
config.terminal.fontFallback.bundledFace: Used only for characters the chosen font lacks, and only for those this family itself has. Requires this family's own font extension; when that isn't installed the setting has no effect (no error, and no fallback).
config.terminal.fontSize: Font size (px) for the Tmux terminal view. Choose the first option to inherit the integrated terminal's font size. A custom value set in settings.json still works even if it isn't in this list.
config.terminal.fontSize.editorDefault: Inherit `terminal.integrated.fontSize`, then `editor.fontSize` — each only if you set it explicitly — and `14` when neither is set.
config.profiles.command: Shell command run as the session's process, e.g. "claude".
config.profiles.description: Text shown beside the profile in the picker. Defaults to the command.
config.profiles.sessionSuffix: Session-name suffix, as in "<workspace>-<suffix>". Defaults to a slug of the profile name.
config.profiles.updateCommand: Command that updates the profile's tool, e.g. "claude update". When set, an Update button appears in the toolbar for this profile's session. Omit for tools without a single self-update command.
